THE DIFF IS INVERTED — its 11.5% coverage is an overstatement, not an understatement. 49 of 58 lines were called "covered" on broad name-matches that probe shows are food, soap and shoes. VERIFIED false-covered (./ary assort probe, live 2026-08-30): "Automatic upper-arm BP monitor / wrist BP / weighing scale / baby scale / gel pack / hearing aid — covered ₹16,315 (broad 'trust')" = ONE SKU, "Uttam Sugar Trust Classic 1 Kg", filed Salt & Sugar. "Fingertip pulse oximeter — covered, matchQuality SPECIFIC, ₹8,511 ('control')" = Pantene Hair Fall Control shampoo, Personal Care. "Clinic-grade consumables for the campus infirmary — covered ₹9,86,966 ('campus')" = Campus Sports Shoes, Footwear, 43 SKUs. "Absorbent cotton wool — covered, SPECIFIC ('jojo')" = Fiama Lemongrass & Jojoba gel bars. "Compressor nebuliser — dormant, 21 SKUs ('mist')" = Yardley London Mist perfume, Odonil Jasmine Mist, and Cambridge Chemistry workbooks. "Crutches — dormant, 2 SKUs ('flamingo')" = "Flamingo 12Th" (a Class-12 book) + "Jivo Flask Flamingo 1000 Ml". "Assembled first aid kit — covered ₹61,345 ('john')" = probe `first aid`/`firstaid` returns 0 SKUs.
DIRECT PROBES, ALL ZERO MATCHES: `sphygmomanometer omron morepen accusure beurer` 0; `oximeter oximetre spo2` 0; `glucometer lancet lancing accuchek onetouch` 0 (the 7 hits are Melon Strip, Havells Powerstrip, LED Strip, Veet wax strips); `tynor vissco knee lumbar cervical collar splint binder sling crutch walker wheelchair` 0; `gauze crepe bandage micropore leukoplast dressing swab tegaderm` 0; `n95 nitrile latex glove gloves` 0; `pregnancy prega velocit ovulation` 0; `weighing tarazu` 0; `syringe dispovan needle` 0 medical; `electral ors orsl enerzal prolyte` 0 medical.
PURCHASE-LEDGER PROOF (the test the diff never ran): across all 9,284 purchase bills, ALL-TIME, ProductName LIKE any of thermomet/oximet/glucomet/nebuli/bandage/gauze/crepe/tynor/vissco/omron/wheelchair/crutch/walker/syringe/dressing/first aid/bp monitor/micropore returns only nine rows — every one a SALAD DRESSING (Veeba, Cremica, Bdm). ARY has never bought a medical device or a wound dressing in its history.
WHAT DOES EXIST (catalogue-wide LIKE scan over all 21,479 SKUs, the honest "covered" list): Hot Water Bag ₹10,240/12m + Coronation Hot Water Bottle ₹5,950/12m (COVERED — I initially missed these probing 'hotpack' instead of 'hot water', and corrected the estimate down by ₹24,000); Knee Cap ₹8,976/12m, 45 units, 33 on hand (COVERED); Dettol Bandaid ₹4,457/12m, 1,824 loose singles at ₹2.42 (the ONLY wound care in the store); 4 Medicare cotton SKUs ₹1,525/12m, all at ZERO on hand; Cipla Thermometer1 4797, Cipla Thermometer1 4798, Hicks Thermometer — 0 purchase lines, 0 all-time sales, 0 on hand = listed-but-never-stocked ghosts.
CONTEXT THAT MAKES THE GAP REAL: Akal Hospital Baru Sahib IS an ARY customer (60 bills, ₹78,210/12m) — VERIFIED to buy bed sheets, curtains, Havells/Bajaj room heaters, Vaseline and Eveready AA cells, and zero medical supplies. Akal Nursing College (₹76,740), Akal De-Addiction Ward (₹2,31,132), Dr Sheetal Bedi (₹88,323), Dr Madam (₹1,87,204) — all buy groceries, fabric and linen. Clinical demand is physically on campus and 100% of the medical-supply spend leaks off it.
ALSO VERIFIED: no LR41/LR44/CR2032 button cells anywhere — the Electricals `Cell` subgroup is AA/AAA pencil cells only (₹55,475/12m). A thermometer sold here would have no replacement cell.
All figures from a live 12-month window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31; DB current to 2026-08-30 20:30 (post-audit feed, per `ary doctor`).
penetration_assumption:
Population 4,700 residents (the ary CLI's own wallet command assumes 5,000 — I used the lower end of the brief's 4,600-4,800 range). Four lines, each stated before its number.
(A) FIRST-AID CONSUMABLES ~Rs 85,000/yr: "one in four residents (1,175 of 4,700) buys one first-aid item — a band-aid pack, crepe bandage, gauze roll, micropore tape, cotton, antiseptic wipes — once a year at Rs 55 average" = Rs 64,625; PLUS "25 wall-mounted first-aid boxes across hostel wings, 2 canteens, school, university, labs, workshop, warehouse and buses, restocked twice a year at Rs 450" = Rs 22,500. Sanity anchor: ARY today sells Rs 5,982/yr of wound care to 4,700 people = Rs 1.27/resident/yr, against a VERIFIED Rs 93/resident/yr on sanitary napkins (Rs 4,37,439/12m) and Rs 69/resident/yr on OTC medicine. Rs 18.5/resident/yr for first aid is a quarter of the OTC shelf and deliberately conservative.
(B) HOME DIAGNOSTIC DEVICES ~Rs 2,10,000/yr: "165 digital thermometers a year at Rs 220 (3.5% of residents; ~800 households, ~4-year life)" Rs 36,300; "20 non-contact IR thermometers at Rs 900, mostly institutional screening" Rs 18,000; "30 upper-arm BP monitors at Rs 1,600 — ~2,200 adults, ~25% hypertension prevalence gives ~550 hypertensives, ~25% own a cuff, ~5-year life" Rs 48,000; "20 fingertip oximeters at Rs 900 (post-COVID replacement cycle)" Rs 18,000; "20 digital weighing scales at Rs 900" Rs 18,000; "20 glucometer starter kits at Rs 900" Rs 18,000; "10 regular diabetics buying one 50-strip box every ten weeks at Rs 700" Rs 35,000; "8 compressor nebulisers at Rs 1,600 plus Rs 6,000 of replacement masks/tubing" Rs 18,800.
(C) ORTHOPAEDIC + MOBILITY ~Rs 77,000/yr: "1.2% of residents (56 people) buy one support a year — ankle binder, wrist splint, LS belt, cervical collar, arm sling — at Rs 450" Rs 25,200, anchored on the single existing Knee Cap SKU already doing 45 units/yr unpromoted off the Under Garment shelf; "15 walking sticks at Rs 450, 4 folding walkers at Rs 1,800, 3 elbow-crutch pairs at Rs 1,200, 2 folding wheelchairs at Rs 7,000" Rs 31,550; "25 reusable gel hot/cold packs at Rs 250 and 12 electric heating pads at Rs 1,200" Rs 20,650. HOT WATER BAGS ARE EXCLUDED — verified already covered at Rs 16,190/12m.
(D) SMALL ABSENT CONSUMABLES ~Rs 60,000/yr: "1,500 ORS sachets a year at Rs 22 (hill summer, canteens, de-addiction ward)" Rs 33,000; "60 ready-made reading glasses at Rs 250" Rs 15,000; "60 pregnancy test kits at Rs 60" Rs 3,600; "pill organisers, oral dosing syringes and droppers" Rs 8,000.
TOTAL Rs 4,32,000, reported as Rs 4,30,000. That is 0.56% of ARY's Rs 7.70 Cr turnover and would move the health shelf from 0.42% to 0.98% of turnover — the normal band for a general store that is the only shop for 4,700 people.
MARGIN, derived from the purchase ledger where possible: first aid 40% (VERIFIED — Dettol Bandaid latest PurchaseCost Rs 1.416 vs SellingRate Rs 3.00 = 52.8% list, Rs 2.42 realised = 41%); ortho/mobility 31% (VERIFIED — Knee Cap PurchaseCost Rs 110.00 vs SellingRate Rs 160.00, four buys Dec-24 to Oct-25 all 29-31%); small consumables 25.33% (VERIFIED — whole Medicare group, 87 costed SKUs, Rs 3,13,083 sales vs Rs 2,33,788 COGS on latest in-window PurchaseCost; whole store is 15.85% for comparison); DEVICES 20% ASSUMED — there is no ledger evidence because ARY has never bought one, and I took the bottom of the demand research's 20-35% Indian-brand band. Blended 26.7%.
EVERY penetration rate above is my assumption, not an observation. ARY has no sales history in this category to fit against, which is why the size is ESTIMATED and the confidence is medium while the absence itself is VERIFIED.
top_skus: Adhesive bandage PACKS (Band-Aid / Handyplast washproof 10s and 20s, plus a kids' printed) — ARY already sells 1,824 LOOSE band-aids a year at Rs 2.42 each on a VERIFIED 41% realised margin; the demand is proven and is being served at the lowest possible value capture. This is the single lowest-risk line in the category.
Absorbent cotton 25g/100g/500g — ALREADY LISTED (4 Medicare SKUs) and at ZERO on hand today; last purchased Jun-2025. This is a buying decision, not a listing decision.
Crepe / elastic bandage 6cm and 10cm (Tynor, Dyna) — zero SKUs in a township with a school, a university and a sports programme; the classic sprain item and the most-asked-for absent line.
Roller gauze bandage 4/6/10cm + sterile gauze swabs 5x5 and 7.5x7.5 (Datt, Romsons) — zero SKUs, zero purchase history.
Micropore surgical tape 1 inch + zinc-oxide plaster — zero SKUs; the item every dressing above needs to stay on.

Digital clinical thermometer (Dr Morepen / Dr Trust, Rs 150-450) AND the LR41/LR44 button cell beside it — 3 thermometer SKUs are already listed with zero purchase lines all-time; ARY stocks no button cells at all, so a thermometer without its cell will read as a faulty product inside a year.

Wall-mounted metal first-aid box for hostel wings, both canteens, school, university, labs, workshop and buses, on a quarterly restock-and-expiry-check — the recurring institutional line, and Akal Hospital's 60 bills a year prove the buying relationship already exists.
ORS sachets (Electral / Prolyte) and one ready-to-drink — zero SKUs; hill summer, two canteens and a de-addiction ward on campus.
Fingertip pulse oximeter and one entry-level upper-arm BP monitor (Dr Morepen BP-02 / Dr Trust 129, Rs 1,200-2,000) — licence-gated, so second wave, but the highest rupee-per-line in the category.

Glucose test strips 50s in TWO brands plus lancets, sold against a named monthly refill list — the only annuity line here; start only after the counter-side blood-sugar check identifies who the diabetics actually are.
blockers: LICENCE — gates roughly Rs 2,10,000 of the Rs 4,30,000. Thermometers, BP monitors, glucometers, oximeters and nebulisers are notified medical devices; retail sale needs a registration/licence from the HP State Licensing Authority (the MD-42 route under the Medical Devices Rules 2017). NOT-CHECKED — this database holds no licence record and cannot answer it; confirm with the HP Drug Controller before ordering any device. The other ~Rs 2,20,000 (bandages, cotton, gauze, tape, supports, gel packs, ORS, reading glasses, first-aid boxes) needs no drug licence and can start immediately.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH — VERIFIED: ARY's purchase ledger contains zero medical or surgical distributors, all-time. Opening a Tynor/Datt/Romsons line through a Solan or Nahan surgical distributor (50-100 km) is the actual first task and the reason effort is weeks, not days. The buying is trivial once a vendor exists.

AVAILABILITY DISCIPLINE — VERIFIED: 206 of 272 existing Medicare SKUs (76%) have ZERO on hand right now. Adding 54 lines to a shelf that cannot keep three-quarters of its current lines in stock reproduces the store-wide failure. The 4 cotton SKUs are the live proof: listed, last bought Jun-2025, zero on hand, Rs 1,525 of sales. Fix the reorder point for the existing lines in the same pass or this gap re-opens.

THE CAMPUS HOSPITAL IS AN UNMODELLED COMPETITOR — NOT-CHECKED and not answerable from FR8HODBNEW. Akal Hospital, Akal Nursing College and the De-Addiction Ward are all ARY customers, and VERIFIED to buy only linen, heaters and groceries. But whether the hospital dispensary already retails devices and consumables to residents is unknown, and it is the single assumption that could halve the device line (B). Ask before the first device order — this is one conversation, not a study.

ACCESSORY TRAP — VERIFIED: no LR41, LR44, CR2032 or any button cell in the catalogue; the Electricals Cell subgroup is AA/AAA pencil cells only. Stock the cell with the device or do not stock the device.

EXPIRY AND MONSOON HUMIDITY — glucose test strips and sterile dressings carry dated shelf life and Baru Sahib humidity is the standing risk on sterile packs. Small, dated buys only; strips in particular should not be bought ahead of a named refill list.

CAPITAL is NOT a blocker — the whole opening buy is roughly Rs 1.5-2 lakh at cost, and the only real capital item is one wheelchair / walker / crutch set (~Rs 15,000), which the demand research is right to treat as a RENTAL asset at Rs 200-800/month rather than retail stock.
